### 1 — Scene
Skin-on fish fillets over a small salad, scattered with cooked lentils and a few white cheese crumbles.

### 2 — Vessel
A large, roughly square dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation, its area is **3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm²**. Food on adjacent plates is excluded.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight and energy
The fish appears oily, possibly mackerel; its identity and energy density are uncertain. The small white pieces look like feta-style cheese.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked skin-on fish | 24% | 127 × 1.2 = 152 ml | 0.95 | 145 g | 220 | 319 |
| Cooked lentils | 9% | 48 × 0.7 = 34 ml | 0.8 | 27 g | 116 | 31 |
| Leafy greens | 6% | 32 × 2 = 64 ml | 0.15 | 10 g | 20 | 2 |
| Tomato/other salad vegetables | 3% | 16 × 1 = 16 ml | 0.6 | 10 g | 25 | 3 |
| White cheese crumbles | 2% | 11 × 0.45 = 5 ml | 1.0 | 5 g | 265 | 13 |

These allocated areas total **44% of the plate**, consistent with the central food pile. They partition the overlapping ingredients rather than counting the same area twice.

A light oily sheen suggests approximately **3 g oil**, adding **27 kcal**; this is a thin coating, not additional plate coverage.

### 8 — Sanity check
Estimated total: **200 g and approximately 395 kcal**. This is plausible for several thin fish pieces with sparse lentils, leaves and cheese on a mostly empty large plate. Fish type and the amount of oil are the largest uncertainties.
